subject: Finalizing GPU Top-up, Tokens/sec Guarantee & Runtime Fallbacks
messages:
From: Samir Rahman <samir@lighthouse.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@lighthouse.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity top-up during renewal — tokens/sec expectations

Hey Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're getting close to a renewal decision and want to lock in an expansion as part of the next term. High-level asks from our infra and procurement teams:

- Add 8 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs to our reserved pool (for Q3–Q4 traffic).
- Need a firm tokens/sec commitment for the combined pool (baseline + top-up) during business hours (PST) and a fallback plan for regional/instance-level failures.
- Confirmation of lead time to provision the GPUs and any cosigned SOW/ordering steps.

Can you share a proposed commitment sheet we can attach to the renewal? Procurement also wants to see concrete SLO language for both availability and throttling behavior (how you handle spikes > committed tokens/sec).

Appreciate a one-page summary we can circulate internally. Copying procurement for visibility.

—Samir

[Attachment: none]
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rahman <samir@lighthouse.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity top-up during renewal — tokens/sec expectations

Samir — thanks for the clear asks. Summary below and attached is a draft commitment schedule + tokens/sec matrix you can use in the order form.

Short answers up front:
- We can reserve +8 A100-equivalent GPUs for Lighthouse AI starting the first day of the new term (requested start: 2027-07-01).
- Proposed committed throughput: 1,900 tokens/sec sustained across the reserved pool during business hours (PST). Peak burst policy: up to 2,700 tokens/sec for short windows subject to available burst capacity and queueing rules.
- Provisioning lead time: 6–8 weeks from signed amendment + payment; expedited provisioning available for an upfront one-time top-up fee.

What I'm attaching:
- Lighthouse_Commit_Schedule_v3.pdf: line-item schedule that plugs into the renewal (includes start/end dates, pricing, and provisioning SLA).
- tokensps_guarantee_matrix.xlsx: tokens/sec commitments by time window, fallback behaviors, and sample measurement queries.

Suggested SLO language (high level):
- Availability SLO: Reserved pool targeting 99.9% operational time measured weekly at the pool level.
- Throughput Commitment: Aggregate committed tokens/sec (1,900 tps) measured via our trace-based counter with 1-minute aggregation windows; deviations >5% for >15 consecutive minutes trigger automated remediation and escalation credits as defined in the matrix.
- Fallback policy: In sustained overload or capacity loss, requests are routed to a pre-agreed model-variant pool (lower-cost / quantized variant) with a max degradation of 15% P95 latency and documented quality delta; customers are notified and can opt for queued requests instead.

I'll loop Marcus for the runtime/fallback wording; Monica will confirm billing cadence and how the tokens accounting maps to invoice line items.

Next steps: if this looks right, I'll send a tracked PDF addendum for signatures and a short amendment redline for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity top-up during renewal — tokens/sec expectations

Adding a few technical clarifications you might want to include in the addendum text (copying Mina's language into suggested clauses):

1) Measurement anchor: "Committed throughput is measured at the pool egress using Redwood's token emission counter with 60s aggregation. Both parties may query counters; disputes are resolved by mutual audit using retained traces for the prior 30 days."

2) Fallback mechanics: "When a physical GPU node breach occurs causing per-instance capacity loss, requests are re-routed following the policy: (A) automated burst–scale from dedicated spare nodes for up to 10 minutes, (B) automatic model-variant fallback with documented quality deltas, (C) per-minute admitted request throttling with backoff. Redwood will publish failure reasons in the Console events stream and send automated incident notifications."

3) Credits and remediation: "Material deviation (sustained <95% of committed throughput for >60 continuous minutes during business hours) entitles Lighthouse AI to service credits equal to X% of that hour's reserved fee; full credit matrix in the attached spreadsheet."

4) Operational playbook link: include a pointer to the fallback playbook (we keep a sanitized customer-facing copy).

I'll attach a trimmed version of the fallback playbook that is safe for procurement (no internal runbook details).

—Marcus

[Attachment: redwood_fallback_playbook.md]
From: Samir Rahman <samir@lighthouse.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@lighthouse.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity top-up during renewal — tokens/sec expectations

Thanks Mina and Marcus — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement before we route to legal:

- Can you confirm the exact probationary measurement window you use to calculate deviations (Marcus suggested 60s aggregation but procurement wants to confirm "15-minute rolling" or "1-minute sample aggregated over 15 minutes").
- For model-variant fallback, are you able to bind the allowed quality delta to a numeric metric we can reference (e.g., P99 perplexity delta, or a labeled eval set drop)? Procurement is wary of vague "documented quality delta" language.
- Please confirm whether expedited provisioning fee is refundable if Redwood cannot meet the agreed provisioning timeline.

If you can send a short redline or a 1-paragraph answer for each, procurement can include it in our procurement sheet and then I'll circle legal.

—Samir

[Attachment: none]
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rahman <samir@lighthouse.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Capacity top-up during renewal — tokens/sec expectations

Samir — answers below (we kept them concise so procurement can paste into the procurement sheet).

1) Measurement window: We measure tokens/sec with 60s counters and report deviations as a 15-minute rolling average (i.e., 15 consecutive 1-minute aggregates). The commit is defined against the 15-minute rolling average during business hours.

2) Quantified fallback quality delta: For model-variant fallback we will bind the allowed quality change to Lighthouse's evaluation set (we propose the Lighthouse-3 eval set you shared in the onboarding packet). Language we can include: "Fallback variants will not exceed a P99 perplexity increase of 12% on the mutually agreed Lighthouse-3 eval set; additional tolerances for task-specific metrics can be appended as schedule items." If you prefer a different metric, we can swap it in the addendum.

3) Expedited provisioning fee refund: Expedited provisioning fee is refundable if Redwood fails to deliver the added GPUs within the agreed provisioning window plus a 7-day cure period, excepting force majeure. We can include a pro-rated refund schedule in the SOW.

Attached is a one-page addendum (PDF) with these bullets as redline-ready clauses and the tokens/sec matrix. If this looks good, I'll generate a tracked PDF and a DocuSign link for signatures.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm the Lighthouse-3 eval set for the quality binding (reply OK).
- Procurement to confirm whether they want the expedited provisioning refund clause as stated or with a shorter cure window.
- We'll prepare the DocuSign package and route to your procurement + legal.

Thanks — Mina

Mina Haddad
